body_html:
Visitors from many countries can enter Vietnam without a visa, but only for a temporary stay with a fixed end date. Anyone planning to hire a motorbike on that kind of entry needs to know where the end date comes from, how to confirm it and what the official sources say about going past it. This article covers the stay limits named on official pages, which nationalities those pages list, and how to fit a rental inside the permitted stay.

The country lists below come from the two government resolutions described on the pages reviewed. They are not a full list of exempt nationalities, and No source reviewed gives the portal's full list. The only other nationalities the sources address are Australia and Canada, whose governments say their passport holders need a visa. For any other nationality, check the official portal's list and any treaty-based exemption. The official portal's own list, and any treaty-based exemptions, should be checked on the official site. The portal page and the Vietnam Tourism (vietnam.travel) pages show no date, so this article reflects them as read on 24 October 2026.

How long the visa-free stay lasts

Vietnam's national e-visa portal, on a page that shows no date, says that citizens of countries unilaterally exempted from visas by Viet Nam are granted a 45-day temporary residence certificate on entry. For people exempt under an international treaty, the stay is whatever the treaty sets, and the portal says a 30-day period is granted where the treaty sets none. For unilateral visa-free entry, the portal also says the passport must be valid for at least another six months.

Which nationalities the official pages name

The Vietnam Tourism (vietnam.travel) pages describe two resolutions. The table sets them side by side, because they do not say the same thing about the purpose of the visit.

ResolutionCountries namedPeriod in forceStay and purpose
44/NQ-CP, issued 7 March 2025Germany, France, Italy, Spain, the United Kingdom, Russia, Japan, South Korea, Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Finland15 March 2025 to 14 March 202845 days from the date of entry, regardless of passport type and purpose of entry, if entry conditions under Vietnamese law are met
229/NQ-CP, dated 11 August 2025Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia and Switzerland15 August 2025 to 14 August 2028Up to 45 days from the date of entry, described as being for tourism purposes, if entry conditions are met

Vietnam Tourism (vietnam.travel) says the first policy will be considered for extension under Vietnamese law when it ends. Both policies are time-limited, so the dates above are a reason to check the current position rather than a promise about it.

Visa-free entry depends on nationality. Australia's Smartraveller advice, updated on 24 September 2026, says Australian passport holders cannot get a visa on arrival, and the Government of Canada, in travel advice last updated 19 October 2026, says Canadian passport holders must have a visa to enter Vietnam. Travellers whose nationality is not named on any official list should read their own government's advice and the official portal.

Your exit date is the one in the passport

The UK government's entry requirements page for Vietnam, which shows no date, tells British visitors they can enter without a visa for up to 45 days for tourism or business. It says the passport is stamped on arrival with the date by which the visitor has to leave. It advises checking that this date is 45 days from the arrival date, and adds that immigration will not change it after the visitor has left the airport or land border.

The UK page describes the exit stamp for British visitors on a visa-free stay. Australia's Smartraveller advice describes the same exit-date stamp for visa holders and warns that a wrong date can lead to an overstay fine. Neither says whether the day of arrival itself counts. For anyone on a visa-free stay, a date written in the passport is better evidence than a personal tally, and any doubt about it is easiest to raise while still at the border.

Planning a rental around the exit date

No source reviewed says anything about renting or riding a motorbike on a visa-free stay, so the points below are planning advice, not rules.

  • Note the stamped exit date as soon as the passport is returned at the border, and compare it with any rental dates before booking.
  • Choose a rental that ends before the exit date, and leave a margin for the trip home.
  • Remember that a longer rental does not lengthen a stay. Motorbike Hire Hanoi: How to Extend Your Rental Period covers extending a rental period, but questions about the permitted stay go to the immigration authorities.
  • Treat visa status as one set of papers among several. Licences are a separate matter, covered in Vietnam Driving Licence Classes A1 and A Explained for Motorbike Renters Under the 2025 Rules, and the bike's papers are another, covered in Rental Motorbike Registration in Vietnam: Match the Bike to Its Papers.

What happens after the exit date

Two official sources are blunt about overstaying. The UK government's guidance on living in Vietnam, last updated 23 September 2025, says overstaying a visitor visa is a serious matter: the traveller may be delayed from leaving until a fine is paid and may be prevented from visiting Vietnam again. The UK entry requirements page says authorities can prevent departure until a fine is paid for overstaying a visa or working illegally, and that the traveller could be deported and barred from future visits.

Whether a visitor can leave and re-enter to begin a new visa-free period, whether any gap between visits applies and whether a visa-free stay can be extended are all questions the sources reviewed do not answer. They should be put to the official portal or the nearest Immigration office rather than assumed.

If you need longer than 45 days

The same UK guidance says that anyone who wants to stay in Vietnam must do so legally and with the right visa, and that visa-related enquiries go to the nearest Immigration office. It also notes that the UK government cannot control the services or rates of commercial visa companies that some foreigners use to extend a stay without leaving the country. Smartraveller describes the e-visa as allowing eligible travellers to stay up to 90 days if it is granted. The e-visa has its own entry and exit rules, and the portal is the place to read them.

Rules on stay lengths and eligible countries change, so confirm the current position with the official source before booking a long rental.

Sources checked

  • Immigration Department, Ministry of Public Security, Viet Nam National Electronic Visa system: unilateral and treaty-based temporary stay, six-month passport rule (no date shown). https://evisa.gov.vn/
  • UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office, entry requirements for Vietnam: 45-day visa-free visits, exit stamp, overstaying (no date shown). https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/vietnam/entry-requirements
  • Vietnam Tourism (vietnam.travel), article on visa waivers for citizens of 12 countries under Resolution 44/NQ-CP (no date shown). https://vietnam.travel/things-to-do/viet-nam-waives-visas-citizens-12-countries
  • Vietnam Tourism (vietnam.travel), article on visa exemption policies effective 15 August 2025 under Resolution 229/NQ-CP (no date shown). https://vietnam.travel/things-to-do/new-visa-exemption-policies-effective-15-august-2025
  • UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office, living in Vietnam: overstaying and enquiries about longer stays (last updated 23 September 2025). https://www.gov.uk/guidance/living-in-vietnam
  • Australian Government Smartraveller, Vietnam: visa position for Australian passport holders and the e-visa (updated 24 September 2026). https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/destinations/asia/vietnam
  • Government of Canada, Vietnam travel advice: visa requirement for Canadian passport holders (last updated 19 October 2026). https://travel.gc.ca/destinations/vietnam

Thuê xe máy Nguyễn Hà is open 09:00–21:00 daily at Ngõ 5 Nguyễn Văn Cừ, Bồ Đề, Long Biên, Hà Nội (near Gia Lâm bus station). Phone: 0334 699 969.
